meta.title: Mr. Barker Goes to Washington
meta.subtitle: A Satirical Congress Micro-Sim
meta.worldNote: Everyone in Maple Creek and Washington can be any animal—teachers, bakers, librarians, and lawmakers alike. The Capitol power brokers you collide with just happen to lean into classic literary fables, while every bill satirizes purely how Congress functions.

artDirection.description: Crisp flat-graphic editorial print aesthetic inspired by Aviary Attorney: warm parchment paper, thick charcoal ink outlines, flat block shading, subtle newspaper halftones, bold congressional crimson, navy, brass gold, and ink black.

platformMadLibs.promptHeader: Congratulations on your upset victory, Representative Barker!
platformMadLibs.promptSubhead: What was your winning campaign platform? Pick one line for each blank—your victory speech shapes your starting standing, your living Flagship Bill, and which House caucuses back you on Day 1.

slots.leadIn: Maple Creek sent me to Washington because...

options.text: "Build more schools, build more roads, build, build, build!"
"Maple Creek deserves a leader who gets things done!"
"The Northern Moose Menace cannot be left unchecked!"

slots.leadIn: And on Capitol Hill, I vow to...

options.text: "Work with anyone to deliver for Maple Creek!"
"Bring every federal dollar I can back to town!"
"Never owe a dime to K-Street lobbyists!"
"Keep my options open and my bow tie spotless!"

slots.leadIn: My signature bill in Congress will champion...

options.billTitle: The National Arts, Libraries & Youth Parks Act
options.billSummary: Funds small-town arts grants, public library wings, and neighborhood playgrounds nationwide—with Maple Creek as an inaugural showcase town.

options.billTitle: The Heartland Job Creation & Small Business Act
options.billSummary: Launches federal trade-apprenticeship grants and streamlined revitalization loans for main-street shops and regional builders.

options.billTitle: The Working-Household & Senior Tax Relief Act
options.billSummary: Cuts federal excise taxes on home heating, expands senior retirement deductions, and simplifies small-shop quarterly tax filings.

options.text: "Clean Rural Power Grids & Regional Rail Transit"
options.billTitle: The Clean Grid & Rural Transit Modernization Act
options.billSummary: Upgrades rural electric grids, lowers household utility bills, and connects small towns to modern regional transit.

options.text: "Build, Build, Build: Federal Clinics, Roads & Courthouses"
options.billTitle: The National Civic Construction & Public Safety Act
options.billSummary: Invests $50B in rural health clinics, county road resurfacing, and modern public safety centers—delivering thousands of construction jobs.

options.billTitle: The Federal Northern Moose-Proofing & Rural Barrier Act
options.billSummary: Establishes a high-visibility federal task force for reinforced highway wildlife crossings, emergency horn whistles, and suspiciously generous moose-spotter stipends.

caucuses.label: Your Freshman Base
caucuses.focus: Your own vote and closest rookie allies—always pledged AYE.

caucuses.label: Children & Conservation
caucuses.focus: Backs schools, clean waterways, public parks, and healthcare.

caucuses.label: Good-Government Sunshine
caucuses.focus: Rewards reading fine print, rejecting sneaky riders, scrubbing redactions, and staying clean.

caucuses.label: Retiree & Fiscal Watchdogs
caucuses.focus: Defends senior pensions, rural post offices, and fiscal restraint.

caucuses.label: Main Street & Builders
caucuses.focus: Champions rail depots, local jobs, small shops, and highway freight.

caucuses.label: Backbench Wildcards
caucuses.focus: Loves bold maverick moves, sharp press clips, and checking the Northern Moose Menace.

caucuses.label: Appropriations & Leadership
caucuses.focus: Hard to win organically—flipped via caucus loyalty, banked Favors, or weighted compromises.

wolf.label: Whip Fang's Caucus Whip Operation (+12 Seats)

grassrootsPush.label: Launch Clean Hometown Call-In Blitz
grassrootsPush.description: Zero corruption! Mobilizes Maple Creek voters to flood congressional switchboards. Seat flip scales with your 3-bloc hometown standing.

weightedCompromises.label: Minor Committee Compromise (+6 Seats)
weightedCompromises.description: Softens compliance deadlines to win over fence-sitters. Clean, small nudge if you're just shy of 51.

weightedCompromises.label: Attach Troughman's Interstate Ramp Earmark (+12 Seats)
weightedCompromises.description: Tucks a $220M federal highway ramp for Troughman's state into your bill. Medium seat boost, stings Seniors.

weightedCompromises.label: Let Whip Fang Co-Brand as a Leadership Bill (+16 Seats)
weightedCompromises.description: Leadership puts its crest across your bill and whips 16 seats—trading independent credibility at home.

weightedCompromises.label: Slip in Viper's Industry Deregulation Rider (+22 Seats & +Funds!)
weightedCompromises.description: Massive K-Street buyout: flips 22 seats AND fills your War Chest, at heavy hometown & Ethics Board cost.

failOutcome.headline: HEARTBREAK ON THE FLOOR! BARKER'S {FLAGSHIP_TITLE} DIES SHORT OF 51 SEATS!
failOutcome.subhead: Too many grey dots on the House hemicycle leave the freshman's signature promise stalled in chamber history.

passOutcome.headline: HOUSE MAJORITY! BARKER PASSES {FLAGSHIP_TITLE} WITH {SEAT_COUNT} VOTES!
passOutcome.subhead: Maple Creek erupts in cheers as Rep. Barker's signature legislation crosses the 51-seat threshold on the House floor.

voterBlocs.label: Families
voterBlocs.priorities: Public schools, clean water, safe parks, and affordable everyday essentials.

voterBlocs.label: Seniors
voterBlocs.voice: Old Man Boarwell (Pig), Retired Postal Carrier
voterBlocs.priorities: Fixed-income tax stability, neighborhood post offices, healthcare copays, and clean oversight.

voterBlocs.label: Main Street
voterBlocs.voice: Sal Viper (Snake), Main Street Sourdough Bakery
voterBlocs.priorities: Local jobs, foot traffic, bridge & rail access, and manageable small-shop taxes & rules.

stafferReport.marginOfErrorNote: Internal office pulse check — qualitative estimates only (roughly ±8% fog of war).

barker.name: Rep. Barnaby Barker
barker.visualBrief: Earnest golden-tan floppy-eared freshman puppy in a slightly oversized off-the-rack navy suit, polka-dot bow tie, perked hopeful ears (droop when stressed).

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Build a 51-seat House coalition for your signature bill and win reelection in Maple Creek.
rolodex.watchOut: Check your MY BILL folder on the desk every week—minor reps pledge or pull House seats based on how you vote!

sheep.name: Martha Ewe
sheep.visualBrief: No-nonsense community organizer with curly cream wool, round brass spectacles, forest-green knit cardigan, holding a town-hall clipboard.

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Clean, transparent federal bills that deliver for everyday hometown voters without hidden traps.
rolodex.watchOut: When a bill splits Families, Seniors, and Main Street, even Martha looks conflicted—read your postcards and Toby's memo!

wolf.name: Whip Fenrir Fang
wolf.visualBrief: Razor-sharp slate-gray wolf in a crisp charcoal pinstripe suit, crimson power tie, brass monocle, gleaming whip-count clipboard.

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Strict Caucus loyalty on leadership bills and must-pass omnibuses—no surprise defections.
rolodex.watchOut: His Favor flips 12 House seats on your Flagship Bill—but sink into Backbench Exile and he'll pull 5 Establishment seats against you.

snake.name: Vesper Viper, Esq.
snake.visualBrief: Sleek emerald viper in a tailored brocade waistcoat, gold pocket-watch chain, tinted pince-nez glasses, calm unblinking poise.

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Favorable deregulation, buried inspection waivers, and quiet NAY votes on bills threatening his clients.
rolodex.watchOut: Holds the keys to your War Chest—and if Maple Creek votes you out while you're flush with his cash, K-Street always has a yacht waiting.

pig.name: Rep. Wilbur Troughman
pig.visualBrief: Portly pink-and-cream veteran lawmaker in a burgundy three-piece waistcoat, brass suspenders, handlebar tusks, waving a gold fountain pen.

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Earmarks, concrete contracts, and old-fashioned vote trading ('you back my project, I'll back yours').
rolodex.watchOut: His riders look ugly on paper, yet occasionally bring real local jobs—and his Favor flips 10 Appropriations seats on your bill.

bear.name: Chairwoman Beatrice Kodiak
bear.visualBrief: Imposing brown bear in a structured tweed blazer, tortoiseshell spectacles, pearl pin, resting one paw on a massive oak gavel.

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Institutional integrity, thorough reading of redacted clauses, and lawmakers with spine.
rolodex.watchOut: Never try to haggle with her—earn her Favor (+9 clean Sunshine seats!) and her Election Night endorsement by exposing hidden ink.

bird.name: Mags Magpie
bird.visualBrief: Sharp black-and-white magpie in a belted trench coat, tilted fedora with a 'PRESS' card tucked in the band, vintage flash-bulb camera.

rolodex.office: Capitol Press Gallery (Staking Out the Coatroom)
rolodex.whatTheyWant: Scandals, contradictions, and live hallway soundbites that sell morning papers.
rolodex.watchOut: Pick a quote matching your actual vote, then nail the Live-Mic timing bar so you don't flinch under her flash bulb!

fox.name: Sterling Foxworth
fox.visualBrief: Impossibly polished russet fox with focus-grouped coiffed fur, tailored navy blazer over cream turtleneck, blinding campaign smile.

rolodex.whatTheyWant: Your congressional seat—and any awkward vote he can splice into a 30-second prime-time attack ad.
rolodex.watchOut: Once he enters the race in Week 7, running low on War Chest funds lets his unanswered billboards drain every Maple Creek bloc weekly.

constituentPostcards.sender: Mrs. Lupine (Wolf), 3rd-Grade Teacher — Maple Creek Elementary
constituentPostcards.note: We heard Washington is voting on $40B in federal school & street grants! Parents are hopeful Maple Creek gets a slice—though retirees here are nervous about how Congress plans to pay for it!

constituentPostcards.sender: Sal Viper (Snake), Owner — Main Street Sourdough Bakery
constituentPostcards.note: Folks are split on that Federal Clean Waterways Act, Barnaby! Families love cleaner rivers and toll-free federal crossings, but our riverside workshops say national filter mandates could squeeze them dry.

constituentPostcards.sender: Sal Viper & Hector Badger — Maple Creek Merchants
constituentPostcards.note: Heads up: the National Rail Corridor bill puts a regional federal depot right outside Maple Creek—150 local jobs! Even if Troughman stuffed ugly earmarks in it, downtown shops WANT this passed!

constituentPostcards.sender: Old Man Boarwell (Pig), Retired Postal Carrier
constituentPostcards.note: Small shippers love cheaper federal parcel rates, sure—but scrub the redactions on that Postal Restructuring bill! Word says Congress is closing 1,400 rural post offices—including ours!

constituentPostcards.sender: Mrs. Lupine & Penny Mallard — Joint Maple Creek Note
constituentPostcards.note: Downtown shops really need federal SBA disaster loans and seniors need winter heating aid, Barnaby—just PLEASE read Page 3 before deciding what Washington is cutting!

constituentPostcards.sender: Old Man Boarwell & Sal Viper — Joint Maple Creek Note
constituentPostcards.note: Retirees are praying Congress caps prescription copays in H.R. 512 today—meanwhile downtown shops are terrified a sneaky payroll tax rider got tucked in to pay for it!

constituentPostcards.sender: Dr. Oona Owl (Owl), High School Civics Teacher
constituentPostcards.note: We tried diagramming H.R. 615 on the chalkboard and broke three pieces of chalk. Read your Staff Legal Memo—and watch out for that slick Fox buying billboards along Highway 9!

constituentPostcards.sender: Sal Viper & Coach Bruno Bear — Maple Creek Diner
constituentPostcards.note: Foxworth's glossy ads are everywhere! Careful with today's Federal 'Ethics' bill—rumor says the redacted fine print slaps $5,000 FEC audit fees on tiny town potlucks and chamber mixers.

constituentPostcards.sender: Old Man Boarwell (Pig) — Maple Creek Watchdogs
constituentPostcards.note: Truckers are furious about Highway 9 detours, so Main Street wants that Federal Highway Trust Fund passed fast—but Chairwoman Kodiak warned us Page 3 hides 75-year no-bid contracts!
Polls open at sunrise! Congress's midnight Shutdown bill locks in a federal Senior COLA boost—but rumor says an 11:58 PM rider slashes school lunches and SBA shop grants to pay for it.

leadOverride.headline: FRESHMAN PUPPY SWORN IN TO REPRESENT MAPLE CREEK!
leadOverride.subhead: Earnest newcomer Rep. Barnaby Barker takes the oath on Capitol Hill as veterans sharpen their pencils for opening week.

policyWatch.headline: Midnight 'Pay-For' Rumored on $40B School Grant Bill
policyWatch.body: Cloakroom clerks spotted leadership staff paper-clipping an eleventh-hour funding offset onto H.R. 101—rumored to hit heating fuel and retirement deductions.

oddity.headline: Local Squirrel Forgets Where He Buried 401(k) Acorns; Blames 'Seasonal Volatility'
oddity.body: Financial advisors urge savers to diversify across at least three separate oak trees before November frost sets in.

policyWatch.headline: Riverside Workshops Brace Ahead of Clean Waterways Vote
policyWatch.body: With last week's opening vote still echoing in Maple Creek, K-Street lobbyists are circling H.R. 118—warning federal runoff rules could squeeze small mills.

oddity.headline: Morning Commute Snarled After 60 Ducks Insist on Merging Single-File at 1 MPH
oddity.body: Drivers reported a 45-minute delay on Route 9, though highway officials concede the flock 'technically used their blinkers.'

policyWatch.headline: Freight Rail Corridor Sparks Rare Town Split Over Jobs vs. Noise
policyWatch.body: Main Street shopkeepers are lobbying hard for the 150 depot jobs inside H.R. 204, even as Appropriations insiders quietly attach a $380M concrete earmark.

oddity.headline: Town Council Debates Whether Owls Working Night Shifts Count as 'Morning People'
oddity.body: A four-hour hearing ended inconclusively after half the committee nodded off at 10 AM and the other half at 8 PM.

policyWatch.headline: Redacted Postal Overhaul May Shutter 1,400 Rural Branches Nationwide
policyWatch.body: Rules Chairwoman Beatrice Kodiak warned freshmen to inspect blacked-out clauses in H.R. 312—and check their own Flagship co-sponsor counts as Floor window opens!

oddity.headline: Controversy Erupts After Raccoon Food Critic Awards Five Stars to Alley Behind French Bistro
oddity.body: The chef called the review 'insulting,' though patio reservations near the service door are now booked solid through winter.

policyWatch.headline: Capitol Printers Jammed as Clerks Wheel Out 1,204-Page Budget Monster
policyWatch.body: Leadership folded SBA storm loans, rural ambulances, and mystery Page-1,204 offsets into one vote—while Mags Magpie camps outside the chamber doors.

oddity.headline: Area Golden Retriever Accidentally Elected HOA President After Enthusiastically Agreeing With Every Motion
oddity.body: Neighbors admit zero bylaws have been passed yet, 'but meeting morale is up 400 percent.'

policyWatch.headline: Rural Telehealth & Copay Cap Bill Faces Last-Minute Payroll Rider
policyWatch.body: Senior groups are cheering H.R. 512's lower prescription costs, while small-business advocates sound alarms over a rumored 2% payroll surcharge buried in Amendment #8C.

oddity.headline: House Dining Room Out of Salmon Again; Three Senators Deny Hoarding Allegations
oddity.body: A terse joint press release stated 'hibernation prep is strictly bipartisan' before aides wheeled away four covered trays.

policyWatch.headline: Mystery Billboards Blanket Highway 9 as Procedural Grammar Trap Looms
policyWatch.body: A dazzlingly coiffed challenger is teasing a primary run just as Leadership drops a quadruple-negative House motion designed to trip hasty voters.

oddity.headline: Startup Unveils $12M 'Whisper-Quiet' Commuter Wheel for Hamsters; Still Goes Nowhere at 30 MPH
oddity.body: Venture backers praised the brushed-aluminum finish before noticing the prototype is bolted to a desk.

policyWatch.headline: Final Week for Freshman Flagship Bills as 'Federal Ethics' Act Hits Floor
policyWatch.body: Watchdogs warn redacted FEC clauses in H.R. 722 squeeze town potlucks while shielding anonymous shells—and any freshman who hasn't called their Flagship vote must do so now!

oddity.headline: Six-Year Study Confirms 92% of Cats Demanding to Go Outside Immediately Demand to Come Back Inside
oddity.body: Exhausted researchers concluded the feline electorate remains 'fundamentally undecided on doors.'

policyWatch.headline: Kodiak Signals Rare Endorsement Ahead of Highway Trust Fund Showdown
policyWatch.body: Freight detours have Main Street demanding quick passage of H.R. 840, yet rumors swirl of a 75-year no-bid procurement rider buried on Page 3.

oddity.headline: Chameleon Political Pundit Blends Into Studio Curtains; Cable Anchors Interview Lamp for 11 Minutes
oddity.body: Focus groups later praised the lamp's fiscal commentary as 'warm, steady, and refreshingly grounded.'

policyWatch.headline: Midnight Government Shutdown Clock Ticks Hours Before Polls Open
policyWatch.body: Congress races to tie an emergency Senior COLA boost to an 11:58 PM Manager's Amendment—forcing one final coalition test before Election Day.

oddity.headline: Veteran Groundhog Declines to Predict Tomorrow's Election After 'Last Winter's Shadow Fiasco'
oddity.body: The forecaster told reporters he is stepping back from political punditry to focus full-time on heirloom turnips.

endings.title: SUBPOENAED BEFORE THE CONFETTI DROPS
endings.headline: BREAKING: ETHICS BOARD RAIDS BARKER VICTORY PARTY OVER 'MYSTERY ESPRESSO MACHINE'
endings.subhead: You played the backroom game recklessly and got sloppy on camera—even K-Street is shredding your phone number.
endings.epilogue: Mags Magpie wins a national journalism award for printing your sticky-note trail. Whip Fang issues a three-word statement: 'Barely met him.'

endings.title: THE ACCIDENTAL SPEAKER
endings.headline: SHOCK ON CAPITOL HILL: FRESHMAN BARKER UNANIMOUSLY DRAFTED AS SPEAKER!
endings.subhead: Zero broken promises, broad Maple Creek support, a passed Flagship Bill, and Kodiak's seal—you pulled off the rarest feat in Congress.
endings.epilogue: Pundits spend months wondering how a wide-eyed rookie unified Families, Seniors, Main Street, and the Caucus without selling out.

endings.title: THE HOMETOWN COALITION CHAMPION
endings.headline: MR. BARKER GOES BACK TO WASHINGTON! MAPLE CREEK VOTERS DEFY THE MACHINE!
endings.subhead: With low corruption and a rock-solid hometown coalition, you proved a freshman can pass a clean bill and win without selling out.
endings.epilogue: Sal Viper brings cinnamon rolls, Mrs. Lupine's class sends banners, and Whip Fang quietly moves your desk away from the radiator.

endings.title: MASTER OF THE MACHINE
endings.headline: MAPLE CREEK BAFFLED AS BARKER WINS REELECTION ON 40,000 GLOSSY ATTACK ADS
endings.subhead: Half your hometown blocs were fuming, but disciplined press spin, donor cash, and party muscle carried you across 50%.
endings.epilogue: Your desk is solid mahogany now. You still keep Mrs. Lupine's faded class card in a drawer—right behind the velvet briefcase.

endings.title: THE UNPREDICTABLE COALITION BUILDER
endings.headline: SPLIT TICKET SHOCKER: NOBODY KNOWS WHAT BARKER WILL DO NEXT—AND VOTERS CAN'T LOOK AWAY!
endings.subhead: You traded votes, stitched together an unlikely Maple Creek coalition, and survived by keeping every faction guessing.
endings.epilogue: Columnists spend all winter debating whether you're a principled independent or a sly horse-trader. Even Toby Otter isn't totally sure.

endings.title: THE GOLDEN PARACHUTE
endings.headline: VOTED OUT AT 8 PM—HIRED BY K-STREET AT 8:05 PM! BARKER SPOTTED SIPPING MARGARITAS ON VIPER'S YACHT!
endings.subhead: Maple Creek sent you packing, yet saying yes to all the right backroom deals landed you a seven-figure 'Senior Policy Advisor' gig with zero floor votes.
endings.epilogue: Your blender never stops whirring, your bow tie is now a Hawaiian shirt, and Rep. Troughman already texted asking if you're free for golf Thursday.

endings.title: ONE-TERM IDEALIST
endings.headline: TOO CLEAN FOR THE AIRWAVES? BARKER LOSES SEAT DESPITE HOMETOWN GOODWILL
endings.subhead: Your integrity stayed spotless, but an empty War Chest and cold Caucus ties let Sterling Foxworth own every billboard in Maple Creek.
endings.epilogue: You head home with your tail high, a standing ovation at the diner, and a hit civics podcast called 'Wait, Did You Read Page 1,204?'

endings.title: OUT-FOXED AT THE POLLS
endings.headline: PRIMARY UPSET! STERLING FOXWORTH SWEEPS MAPLE CREEK AS BARKER COALITION FRACTURES
endings.subhead: Caught between split local blocs and vengeful Capitol insiders, your winning coalition collapsed before Election Night.
endings.epilogue: Within 48 hours, Vesper Viper slips an embossed business card under your door: 'Need a consulting gig, kid? Former reps make wonderful lobbyists.'

civicReceipts.summary: No representative's district agrees on everything: families, retirees, and local businesses often have genuinely competing interests on the exact same bill, forcing lawmakers to build workable coalitions rather than chasing 100% approval.

Passing legislation requires assembling a 51%+ House majority across competing caucuses—either by earning organic co-sponsors through consistent votes and public pressure, or by trading favors and compromises.
Controversial funding offsets or policy riders are routinely attached to popular bills right before a vote, forcing lawmakers to weigh real local benefits against painful fine print.
Combining hundreds of unrelated measures into one giant must-pass bill squeezes out amendment debate and guarantees critics can attack whichever way a representative votes.
Passing a signature bill often requires adding targeted funding or concessions for colleagues' priorities—trading legislative purity to build a working floor majority.
Procedural motions and ballot phrasing are sometimes written in nested negatives so that voting 'Aye' achieves the opposite of what the friendly title suggests.

civicReceipts.term: Caucus Whips, Ad Wars & Primary Challengers
civicReceipts.summary: Leadership enforces discipline via committee assignments and endorsements, while running out of campaign funds leaves even popular lawmakers vulnerable to unanswered primary attack ads.
Complex legislative trade-offs rarely fit in a brief hallway clip, rewarding lawmakers who frame their votes clearly before opponents define them first.
